findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_fx_events · Private data: request_free_key · Public sink: get_unmet_demand, get_rate_stack, request_free_key · Destructive: get_stress_signals, get_methodology.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_fx_events · Private data: request_free_key · Public sink: get_unmet_demand, get_rate_stack, request_free_key · Destructive: get_stress_signals, get_methodology

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_hourly" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "The street rate of a currency per UTC hour for one day, with the day's summary (vwap, high, low, hours, busiest hour). Pro and Enterprise keys; hours arrive with the daily update." → after: "The street rate of a currency per UTC hour for one day, with the day's summary (vwap, high, low, hours, busiest hour), for every currency with hourly market data; each hour says its component (transaction_based / multi_source / combined) and quality. Pro and Enterprise keys."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
